findings.locator: PDF p4 / printed p3, Definition of increasing/decreasing
findings.source_claim: Defines decreasing by a<b implies f(a)<f(b), repeating the increasing inequality.
findings.correction_or_qualification: For strictly decreasing use a<b implies f(a)>f(b).
findings.checked_deduction: The examplef(x)=-x has negative derivative and f(a)>f(b) whenevera<b. The page image confirms the printed less-than sign. The preceding conclusion about negative derivative is correct; its displayed definition is not.

findings.locator: PDF p5 / printed p4, numbered property3 and subsequent exponential bounds
findings.source_claim: Writes e^x>1+x without a domain on the listed claim, and later writes the quadratic truncation bound similarly.
findings.correction_or_qualification: For the displayed derivative-based proof, specify x>0. Globally e^x>=1+x with equality only at0; the quadratic lower bound is not valid for every negative x.
findings.checked_deduction: Atx=0 the claimed strict linear inequality fails by equality. Forx<0, h=e^x-1-x has hprime=e^x-1<0 and decreases to0 asx rises to0, so h>0 there as well. For the quadratic expression atx=-1, e^-1<1/2, reversing the asserted lower bound if it is read without the inherited x>0 restriction.

findings.locator: PDF p2 final paragraph and Fig2 on p3
findings.source_claim: For|x| says a shifted line first touches at0 no matter what its slope is.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Restrict to secants across a<0<b, whose slopes lie strictly between-1 and1, as shown in Fig2.
findings.checked_deduction: Then |x|-mx has a strict minimum at0. For an arbitrary slopem=2 on[-1,1], |x|-2x is minimized atx=1 instead; the unrestricted wording is false. The illustrated cross-corner counterexample to MVT has the intended scope and is correct.

findings.locator: PDF p2 / printed p1, Geometric Proof and Fig1
findings.source_claim: Shifts a parallel line until first contact, using a line from above alternatively.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Explain why an interior contact exists for at least one shift direction; if the curve coincides with the secant, any interior point works.
findings.checked_deduction: Setg=f-l where l is the secant line, sog(a)=g(b)=0. Continuity on the compact interval gives extrema. Ifg is nonzero somewhere, a positive maximum or negative minimum occurs in the interior; differentiability givesgprime(c)=0. Ifg is identically0, the desired slope holds everywhere. A first contact from the wrong direction can occur only at endpoints, so this qualification completes the otherwise valid geometric argument.

findings.locator: PDF p4 / printed p3, three derivative-sign conclusions and proofs
findings.source_claim: Lists derivative-sign and zero-derivative consequences without explicitly saying throughout an interval.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Apply the sign condition at every interior point of an interval, with the continuity needed at any included endpoints.
findings.checked_deduction: MVT compares anytwo points only when the segment between them lies in the domain and satisfies its hypotheses. A function equal0 on(-infinity,0) and1 on(0,infinity) has derivative0 throughout its disconnected domain but is not globally constant. All supplied MVT proofs are valid with the interval condition.

findings.locator: PDF p3 / printed p2, Boston-to-Chicago interpretation
findings.source_claim: Defines f(t) as distance from Boston and identifies fprime with speed.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Use differentiable cumulative distance along the stated1000-mile trip, or explicitly a one-dimensional forward-motion coordinate. Distance from a fixed point in space generally has derivative only the radial velocity component.
findings.checked_deduction: In the intended scalar smooth model, MVT gives fprime(c)=1000/3 mph. A smooth curved1200-mile route traversed at constant400 mph for3h can end1000 miles from its start without ever having speed333.33 mph; radial distance and path length must not be interchanged. The numerical quotient itself is correct.

findings.locator: PDF pp3-4, comparison with linear approximation and Fig3
findings.source_claim: Contrasts MVT with a tangent of definite slope fprime(a).
findings.correction_or_qualification: For that additional linearization, assume a finite derivative at the base pointa; MVT alone requires differentiability only on(a,b).
findings.checked_deduction: f(x)=sqrt(x) is continuous on[0,1] and differentiable on(0,1), so MVT applies, but no finite fprime(0) exists. The smooth illustrated example has the required tangent; this is a scope distinction, not a defect in the MVT statement.

independent_checks.check: Complete attribution page read/inspected; no mathematical content.

The MVT statement correctly includes continuity on[a,b], differentiability on(a,b) anda<c<b, witha<b understood. Secant slope and tangent slope equality correct. Fig1 has a rising secant, parallel shifted lines, and an interior positive-slope tangent; the labelsand directions are consistent. Completed the proof via the compact-interval extremum argument.

Fig2 crosses both branches of|x|, with intermediate secant slope that equals neither derivative-1 nor+1; failure is due to nondifferentiability at0. Recomputed1000/3 mph and identified modeling conditions. Multiplying the MVT equation byb-a and relabelingb=x correctly gives the two exact alternative forms forx>a. Existence does not determine a unique c.

Fig3 correctly depicts the tangent approximation below a convex curve and a vertical discrepancy atx. Positive/negative derivative proofs follow from sign offprime(c)(b-a); zero derivative gives equal values for anypair in the interval. Strictly increasing is a sufficient conclusion forpositive derivative, but the converse is not asserted; e.g.x^3 has a zero derivative at0. The decreasing-definition typo is isolated above.

Forx>0, f1=e^x-1 has positive derivative and value0at0; f2=e^x-1-x has derivativef1>0 and value0at0. Repeating withfn=e^x-sum(k=0..n-1)x^k/k! givespositive remainders forx>0. Printed quadratic and cubic coefficients1/2,1/3! are correct. The infinite-series equality is explicitly deferred rather than proved by the finite bounds; independently a Taylor remainder bound e^|x||x|^(n+1)/(n+1)! tends to0 for fixedrealx, establishing the eventual formula.
